Max Heights Infrastructure Ltd is trading at a significant discount to its asset backing, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.56x based on a share price of ₹ 10.6 against a book value of ₹ 18.9 [E2]. The business is currently hovering near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 14% of the way up from its low of 10 to its high of 17 [E5], presenting an attractive entry point relative to its underlying net worth [E2]. Crucially, the fundamental momentum has turned aggressively positive in the near term, demonstrated by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 212% [E17] and a compounded profit growth of 139% [E21]. This sharp operational acceleration is further reinforced by 3-year compounded sales growth of 29% [E16] and 3-year profit growth of 33% [E20], proving that recent outperformance is building on a multi-year recovery. Conceded: the company carries a 5-year compounded sales contraction of -13% [E15], a 5-year profit contraction of -28% [E19], and a zero dividend yield [E4]. Yet, recent profit growth now exceeds 1-year price growth by 153%, signaling that the market is only just beginning to catch up to a company that is actively outperforming expectations [E48].

Conceded: the company demonstrates a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 212% [E17] and a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 139% [E21], alongside 3-year sales growth of 29% [E16] and profit growth of 33% [E20]. However, the bull's reliance on a 0.56x price-to-book ratio [E2] and its position at 14% of its 52-week range [E5] ignores the reality that asset backing and low relative pricing offer no protection against structurally eroding long-term performance, evidenced by a 5-year sales contraction of -13% [E15], a 5-year profit contraction of -28% [E19], and 10-year profit growth of -2% [E18]. Furthermore, the valuation is heavily inflated despite the recent cyclical bounce, trading at a P/E of 48.1x [E1] or a staggering 249.25x against a sector benchmark of just 23.16x [E6].
